extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of manuscripts submitted to Injury Prevention (and similar biomedical/public-health journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating manuscripts submitted to Injury Prevention: reviewers (three per paper) rate Significance, Appropriateness, Science, and Writing on a three-point scale and give a composite recommendation; editors use these ratings and may convene a committee when recommendations sharply disagree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a three-point scale (high, medium, low). In the author's small sample (20 papers) the mean percent agreement among three reviewers on Significance was 56% (range 0–100, SD 30.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the paper's appropriateness/suitability for the journal Injury Prevention (Appropriateness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a three-point scale (high, medium, low). Reviewers agreed most on this dimension in the sample: mean agreement 69% (range 0–100, SD 28.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific quality, methodology, and validity of the work (Science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a three-point scale (high, medium, low). In the sample mean agreement was 60% (range 0–100, SD 33.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the manner in which the paper is written (clarity, presentation) (Writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a three-point scale (high, medium, low). In the sample mean agreement was 62% (range 0–100, SD 24.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-point rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The rating scale used for each of the four key elements: high, medium, or low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for Significance, Appropriateness, Science, and Writing. The author measured inter-reviewer agreement with a simple percent-agreement rule: all three choosing the same rating = 100% agreement; two choosing the same = 66% agreement; all three different = 0% agreement. The editorial note recommends considering chance agreement statistics (e.g., kappa) although kappa is noted as awkward for the three-reviewer situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite recommendation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give a composite recommendation based on their assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite recommendations include: accept as is (exceptionally rare), provisionally accept, provisionally reject, or reject (relatively common). The manuscript handling workflow treats these composite recommendations as a key input to editorial decisions; sharp disagreement among these recommendations triggers further adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer panel composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard setup of reviewers for each paper and how reviewer input is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each paper is reviewed by three reviewers, one of whom is usually a member of the editorial board. Reviewers convey concerns to authors and provide summaries for the editor. The handling editor uses reviewer comments and recommendations to make the final decision or to refer the paper to a committee when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication for reviewer disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure used when reviewers' composite recommendations sharply disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composite recommendations sharply disagree the handling editor either makes a final decision or refers the paper to a committee comprising the editor, deputy editors, the statistical editor, and the book review editor. The committee step is employed mostly in cases of sharp disagreement. The editorial notes that reviewers' written comments sometimes do not match their composite recommendation strength, which is a factor in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to authors and readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial responsibilities toward authors and readers when using reviewer input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must satisfy both authors (who want minimal hassle) and readers (who want scientific quality and clear writing). Concerns raised by reviewers are conveyed to authors and summarized for the editor. Readers are encouraged to express criticisms post-publication (letters, follow-up papers, direct contact) to help improve the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of reviewer agreement and statistical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewer agreement can and should be measured and contextualized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author used a simple percent-agreement measure for three reviewers but notes that a chance-corrected statistic like kappa would be ideal; kappa is noted as not lending itself easily to the described three-reviewer situation. Expert estimates of chance agreement for two of three reviewers are cited informally (roughly 3.6% to about 10%); the author invites statistically inclined readers to comment on the correct chance-agreement estimate. In the sample of 20 papers, overall mean agreement across the four elements was 56% (overall range 0–75, SD 24.3).
